title: Input an interface rejects before scanning
summary: Inputs an interface declares invalid before scanning: byte sequences that are not UTF-8 (truncated, lone continuation, overlong, encoded surrogate, 0xFF) and a string chunk cut between the two halves of a UTF-16 surrogate pair.
rationale: An expected rejection is neither a detection nor a miss. It has its own denominator (inputValidity other than valid) and no spans, and must not be counted as a true or false negative. Whether and how an interface rejects, with which error code, is the owning product's statement; this record states only that the input is invalid and why.

expectation.rationale: Project policy: a rejection is recorded as input validity, not as a true or false negative; the fixtures carry no spans. The fact that each input is invalid is derived from the bytes (RFC 3629 section 3; Unicode FAQ on surrogates) and is re-checked by the validator. Reverse if a maintainer adds a rejection outcome through a schema decision.

sources.supports: Section 3 prohibits encoding U+D800-U+DFFF: a lone surrogate has no UTF-8 form.
Surrogates are the paired code units of UTF-16 (D800-DBFF leading, DC00-DFFF trailing); an unpaired one cannot be converted to UTF-8 and a converter treats it as an error.
sources.locator: 'What are surrogates?' and 'How do I convert an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate to UTF-8?'

sources.supports: UTF-8 decode: BOM bytes are consumed by decode; invalid sequences become U+FFFD; a streaming TextDecoder keeps an incomplete multibyte sequence buffered across chunks.
sources.locator: sections 6.1, 7.2 and 8.1.1 (Living Standard, last updated 21 May 2026)

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Research for #96 (parent #92). Synthetic fixtures only; input facts and expectations live here, while stream APIs, limits, actual output and rejection assertions belong to downstream engine and product regression populations.
